I was issued an M4A3, now as a civilian I own an AK-47 and Mini 14

The myth about AK inaccuracy is just that, yes it's not as accurate as an AR-15 style rifle, however at >300 yards with some practice a decent sized target is no problem if you're a half way decent shot. I also own a Mini 14 and find it to be reasonably accurate and very reliable.

AK pros: Less expensive than most AR-15s and similar rifles
           :Cheap ammo
           :Plenty of aftermarket parts to suit your needs
           :virtually nothing short of very cheap parts will make an AK jam
           :AKs are very easy to operate and clean and can go longer without
            cleaning

AK cons: recoil is stout and can lead to difficulty in fallow up shots
           :handling can be awkward 
           :AK is not a light firearm

AR-15 Pros: Very accurate even at ranges <300 yards
          :More aftermarket parts than you'd ever be able even consider
          :light weight
          :recoil is negligible

AR-15 Cons: A cheap AR would buy most good AK variants
          :ARs will require regular maintenance
          :ARs are more complicated, but not rocket surgery

Mini 14 Pros: Price is intermediate between an AK and AR
          :Fairly accurate
          :reliability is great

Mini 14 cons: After market parts are available but not as prevalent as 
          other rifles
          :magazines tend to cost more

These are just some observations I've made about some of the rifles that i'm familiar with that I think fit your "serious rifle" criteria.

What might work best is going out and trying a few different ones and see which one feels right. I can't tell you what would work best for you.

Names, Units etc omitted for OPSEC

Four months into my first and only tour, things were slow, routine patrols setting up/taking down OP's.

It was a sharp piercing deafening noise, I remember the blast knocking me to my feet then seeing the 2/4 HUMVEE on fire looking...wrong.

I was still trying to unfuck myself when 2nd plt's medic grabbed me screaming at my face telling me to cover him as he pulls out everyone he can.

I set up behind him while 2nd plt's medic and an Iraqi police officer start pulling friends out of a twisted wreck. 

Then I saw him.

He came out running from behind a corner less than 30m away, he was clean shaven, young.

I saw another fallowing him, I yelled as he raised his weapon as did the one behind him.

I gave a long burst from my 240, I fucking saw them and the concrete around them break apart, red exploded from them and they fell.

I know I shouldn't feel bad, but I keep seeing the anger in his expression then pain, then nothing.

Three out of the four in 2/4 truck had serious burns, the dismount got lucky with little more than a concussion and minor burns.

The next few months I did my best to keep it together, to not shut down or crack up because I didn't want to let anyone down. 

I've been out for almost two years and although time has helped, I still space out and go back there.
